selected_mechanism.name: Terra Energy Center DOE Defense Production Act Coal Grant Stack

news_trigger.what_happened: Trump is using taxpayer money for coal to power AI. Combining funds from the Defense Production Act and 2021's infrastructure law, the $700 million pot will fund new coal plants and an export terminal. The first, a proposed 1.25-gigawatt coal-fired plant in Alaska, would be developed by the Terra Energy Center, an affiliate of Canadian company Flatlands Energy. But the project site is 70 miles from the nearest transmission line, and the mine needed to feed the plant doesn't yet exist.

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: A Defense Production Act-authorized DOE grant to Terra Energy Center Corp. unlocks a proposed 1.25-GW coal-with-carbon-capture plant in the West Susitna watershed — explicitly positioned as AI-data-center baseload — but the plant cannot be built until three independent gates clear sequentially: the Alaska DOT&PF Commissioner's Record of Decision on the West Susitna Access Road EIS, a binding Matanuska Electric Association power purchase agreement, and a greenfield coal mine permit stack.

layers.layer_name: L1 — DOE Defense Production Act Title III Authority
layers.what_it_does: Presidential DPA invocation (50 U.S.C. §4531) authorizes the Department of Energy to channel Defense Production Act Title III funds directly to coal construction projects without a standard competitive grant process, creating the legal hook for the entire grant stack.
layers.controlling_actor: Secretary of Energy (institutional role; current incumbent: Chris Wright); DPA Title III grants require Secretary-level authorization
layers.verification_note: DOE energy.gov newsroom confirmed June 4, 2026 DPA Title III funding announcement for 13 coal capacity projects; Alaska project confirmed as one of four in the companion $350M Restoring Reliability package.

layers.layer_name: L2 — DOE Grant Award to Terra Energy Center Corp.
layers.what_it_does: A DOE grant (reported as $89M federal share, $190.4M with required dollar-for-dollar match) flows to Terra Energy Center Corp. (affiliate of Flatlands Energy, Canada) to fund feasibility, design, and pre-construction work on the 1.25-GW coal plant near Skwentna. The grant is conditional on the project clearing downstream permitting and commercial gates.
layers.controlling_actor: DOE Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations / HGEO (institutional role; administered at the program-office level)
layers.verification_note: DOE energy.gov confirms Anchorage Alaska project is one of four selected in the $350M Restoring Reliability package; Terra Energy Center named as the Alaska recipient in Latitude Media June 4 (fetched) and E&E News March 20 (fetched). Specific $89M project-level breakdown not extractable from DOE primary page; project fact sheet URL returned 404.

layers.layer_name: L3 — West Susitna Access Road NEPA EIS (Chokepoint Layer)
layers.what_it_does: A required approximately 22-mile gravel road crossing more than 180 streams in the West Susitna corridor must be permitted through a full NEPA Environmental Impact Statement before any coal mine can be accessed. The Alaska DOT&PF Commissioner signs the Record of Decision — the binary gate that either opens or closes the mine site to vehicular access. No road ROD = no mine construction start = no coal supply = no power plant.
layers.controlling_actor: Alaska DOT&PF Commissioner Ryan Anderson, P.E. (confirmed on dot.alaska.gov/comm/; authorized ROD signing official for state-led highway EIS under Alaska Admin. Code Title 17)
layers.verification_note: dot.alaska.gov project page confirmed active; describes 22-mile gravel road, ongoing environmental research across soils, hydrology, wetlands, habitats, and archaeological resources, DOT&PF as lead agency. Ryan Anderson confirmed as Commissioner from dot.alaska.gov/comm/. Programmatic Agreement materials released March 17, 2026, project in active NEPA scoping phase.

layers.layer_name: L4 — Matanuska Electric Association Binding Power Purchase Agreement
layers.what_it_does: MEA's board of directors must vote to convert the existing nonbinding term sheet into a binding, long-term power purchase agreement before the project can reach financial close. Without a signed offtake agreement from a creditworthy utility, project debt financing is unavailable regardless of the DOE grant.
layers.controlling_actor: MEA Board of Directors (multi-member; parallel commercial gate, not the primary chokepoint)
layers.verification_note: E&E News March 20, 2026 article (fetched) confirms MEA is working closely with Terra Energy on a nonbinding term sheet for a power purchase agreement. mea.coop news page returned 404.

layers.layer_name: L5 — Greenfield Coal Mine Permitting Stack
layers.what_it_does: A coal mine that does not yet exist must obtain an ADNR mining lease, BLM surface management permit, MSHA mine plan approval, and Alaska DEC air and water permits before it can produce the coal needed to fuel the plant. Each agency holds an independent veto. E&E News quotes: 'Right now, there is no mine.'
layers.controlling_actor: Multiple parallel agencies (ADNR Commissioner, BLM Alaska State Director, MSHA District Manager, ADEC Commissioner) — diffuse multi-agency structure; not a single chokepoint
layers.verification_note: E&E News March 20 confirms no mine exists and describes permitting complexity. Individual agency primary sources not fetched. Layer demonstrates structural dependency but lacks full per-layer primary source coverage.

chokepoint.layer_name: L3 — West Susitna Access Road NEPA EIS
chokepoint.controlling_actor: Alaska DOT&PF Commissioner Ryan Anderson, P.E.
chokepoint.binary_decision: Sign the Record of Decision on the West Susitna Access Road EIS (road construction begins, mine site accessible, plant path opens) OR withhold/remand it (mine cannot be built, plant has no fuel supply, $190M+ investment is stranded)
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: No other actor in the stack — not DOE, not MEA, not any mine permitting agency — can substitute for this gate. The road is the only viable access route to the only viable coal mine site, and the ROD is a single-agency decision under state authority. Army Corps Section 404 for wetlands crossings is a parallel federal gate but the state ROD must come first.
chokepoint.timeline: Currently in active NEPA scoping; Programmatic Agreement materials released March 17, 2026; ROD estimated no earlier than late 2027

selected_mechanism.structural_read: This mechanism is structurally unusual because the chokepoint — a state road EIS — sits two layers downstream from the federal money but is the one gate that cannot be parallelized or waived. DOE can grant, Terra Energy Center can design, investors can commit equity, and MEA can negotiate — none of it moves the mine closer to existence without a road ROD. The Alaska DOT&PF Commissioner's decision is the real option on the entire $190M+ investment stack. The mechanism also reveals that coal-for-AI is not a simple federal-dollars-to-plant pipeline; it requires a greenfield infrastructure buildout in one of Alaska's most logistically demanding corridors, where NEPA, Army Corps wetland jurisdiction, tribal consultation requirements, and state-level permitting each operate on independent timelines measured in years, not months.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Any executive, project manager, or capital allocator treating the DOE grant announcement as a construction-timeline signal should instead be tracking the West Susitna Access Road EIS docket at dot.alaska.gov and the Army Corps Section 404 wetlands permit application — neither of which existed as formal filings as of the June 2026 announcement. The next concrete decision gate is the DOE grant agreement execution (expected within 90 days of June 4 announcement), which will contain the feasibility-study milestones that determine whether Terra Energy Center's pre-development timeline is credible. MEA board members should be pressed this month on whether the nonbinding term sheet will survive a cost-of-power analysis against North Slope gas or Cook Inlet alternatives.
selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Southcentral Alaska's AI data center power capacity — including JBER/Eielson/commercial Railbelt sites identified in the DAF 4,700-acre parcel survey — has no coal-baseload path if the West Susitna Access Road ROD is withheld, delayed beyond 2028, or remanded by Army Corps Section 404 wetlands review. MEA, as the sole utility in nonbinding PPA discussions, must decide in the next 12-18 months whether to convert to a binding offtake agreement before the DOE grant's feasibility-study period expires.
